problems.title: Problem 1: Two circles
problems.problem:
Problem 1: Two circles

In a thick slab made of a non-conducting solid material, a hole of small diameter is drilled perpendicular to the surface; its depth is less than the thickness of the slab. One end of a rubber cord with spring constant $k$ is attached to the "bottom" of the hole. The length of the undeformed rubber cord is exactly equal to the depth of the hole. A bead of mass $m$, carrying a positive charge $q$, is attached to the other end of the cord. The slab is placed horizontally in the gravitational field. The surface of the slab is smooth. A uniform magnetic field is switched on perpendicular to the surface of the slab; its induction vector is directed opposite to the vector of the free-fall acceleration. The magnitude of the magnetic induction is $B$. Stretching the cord, the bead is displaced along the surface of the slab to a distance $r_0$ from the axis of the hole and released, having been given a velocity perpendicular to the cord such that the bead moves along a circle.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2024-1-1-fig1.png

1. Determine the angular velocities of the bead when it rotates clockwise and counterclockwise (as seen from above).

The force acting on the bead depends linearly both on its position $\vec r$ and on its velocity $\vec v$. Therefore, if there are two different laws of motion $\vec r_1(t)$ and $\vec r_2(t)$ describing some motions of the bead, then the equation $\vec r(t)=\alpha\cdot\vec r_1(t)+\beta\cdot\vec r_2(t)$ for any constants $\alpha$ and $\beta$ correctly describes the law of a physically realizable motion of this bead under the action of the same forces (indeed, the velocity and acceleration of the bead at any moment of time will be described by the same combinations). For example, if the bead is released from the same initial position as in part 1 without an initial velocity, its law of motion can be found as the result of superposition of the laws of rotation that you studied in this part.

2. What is the minimum distance from the axis of the hole that the bead will reach after being released without initial velocity from the distance $r_0$ from the hole?

3. After what time $\tau$ after the release will the bead again be at the distance $r_0$ from the axis of the hole?

4. Sketch the trajectory of the bead for the case $q^2B^2/(mk)=1/2$. After what time after the release will the bead be at the initial point for the first time?

problems.title: Problem 2: A mercury pancake
problems.problem:
Problem 2: A mercury pancake

A little mercury is carefully poured onto the upper horizontal base of a solid circular cylinder with cross-sectional area $S$. The contact (wetting) angle of the material of which this cylinder is made is $\theta$. The surface tension coefficient of mercury is $\sigma$, the density of mercury is $\rho$. The free-fall acceleration is $g$. Assume that the parameters $\sigma$, $\rho$, $g$ and $S$ satisfy the inequality:

$$\sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{\rho g}}\ll\sqrt{S}.$$

1. At what minimum volume of mercury $V_0$ will it cover the base of the cylinder completely?

Mercury of volume $V<V_0$ is poured onto the base of the cylinder. A second cylinder with the same cross-section, but made of a different material which is completely non-wetted by mercury, is carefully placed on top. Assume that the arrangement of the cylinders and the mercury is axisymmetric at all times.

2. At what minimum mass $m_1$ of the upper cylinder will the mercury be in contact with the base of the lower cylinder over the whole area of its surface?

3. At what minimum mass $m_2$ of the upper cylinder will the mercury flow out of the gap between the cylinders? Assume that the boundary between the base of the cylinder and its lateral surface is rounded (the radius of rounding is much smaller than the thickness of the mercury layer) and convex.

problems.title: Problem 3: Truncated cone
problems.problem:
Problem 3: Truncated cone

A right solid non-conducting truncated cone is charged over its lateral surface so that its surface charge density depends on the distance to the apex O of the complete cone as $\sigma(x)=A/x$, where $A$ is a known positive constant. The bases of the truncated cone are charged uniformly with surface densities $\sigma_1$ and $\sigma_2$ (see figure). The slant length and the half-angle of the aperture of the cone that completes the truncated cone to a full cone are $l$ and $\alpha=30^\circ$ respectively; the slant length of the truncated cone is $l$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2024-1-3-fig1.png

1. Let $\sigma_1=-\sigma_2=\sigma_0$, where $\sigma_0$ is a known quantity. Find the electric field vector $\vec E_{\mathrm O}$ at point O.

A thin channel is drilled in the cone, so that a negative test charge $-q$ ($q>0$) of mass $m$ can move without friction along the axis of symmetry of the cone. From now on, $\sigma_1=\sigma_2=\sigma_0$.

2. Prove that there exists an equilibrium position of the test charge that does not depend on the value of $\sigma_0$. Find this equilibrium position. Give as the answer its distance from point O.

3. For what values of $\sigma_0$ will the equilibrium position found be stable? For the values corresponding to stable equilibrium, find the period of small oscillations of the test charge near the equilibrium position.

Note: the cone is fixed, the permittivity of the truncated cone is $\varepsilon=1$; neglect the effect of gravity and magnetic phenomena.

problems.title: Problem 4: Frame and wire
problems.problem:
Problem 4: Frame and wire

A rigid rectangular frame made of thin wire can move on a smooth horizontal surface on which a thin, infinitely long straight wire is fixed. The figure shows a top view of this system. Initially the currents in the wire and in the frame are zero. The frame is at rest in such a position that one pair of its sides is parallel to the wire, and the distance between the wire and the side of the frame nearest to it is many times larger than all dimensions of the frame. The current in the wire is increased to a certain maximum value so quickly that the displacement of the frame during the increase of the current can be neglected. After that the current in the wire is kept constant. It turned out that at the moment when the current in the wire reached its maximum value, the speed of the frame was $v_0$. The inductance of the frame can be neglected, and its resistance can be considered constant. What will be the speed $v_1$ of the frame a very long time after the current in the wire reached its maximum value?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2024-1-4-fig1.png

problems.title: Problem 5: Inhomogeneity in a prism
problems.problem:
Problem 5: Inhomogeneity in a prism

The experimenter Glück is carrying out optical investigations with a solid prism whose cross-section OAB is a right triangle with legs AB and $OA=h$. All faces of the prism are either parallel or perpendicular to the plane of the figure. If a rectangular coordinate system $xOy$ with origin at point O is introduced as shown in the figure, the refractive index of the material of the prism depends only on the coordinate $x$ according to the law:

$$n(x)=\frac{3}{2-x/h}.$$

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2024-1-5-fig1.png

Glück decided to illuminate completely the face of the prism that contains OA and is perpendicular to the plane of the figure with a beam of light perpendicular to that face. The bottom of the prism, containing AB and perpendicular to the plane of the figure, is coated with a substance that completely absorbs the light falling on it. The prism is in air, whose refractive index can be taken equal to one. In what follows, consider only the rays that enter the prism through points lying on the side OA of the prism.

1. Consider a ray entering the prism at the point with coordinate $x_0$. Find the equation of the trajectory of this ray inside the prism until it reaches the sides AB and OB of the prism. It is not necessary to find the values of $x$ for which the obtained equation of the trajectory is applicable.

2. For what values of the angle $\angle AOB=\alpha$ do the light rays reach all points of the side OB of the cross-section of the prism?

3. For what values of the angle $\alpha$ are all rays that reached the side OB of the cross-section of the prism refracted and transmitted into the air?

problems.title: Problem 1: Falling into the abyss
problems.problem:
Problem 1: Falling into the abyss

The two opposite walls of a deep gorge are parts of parallel vertical planes. One windless day the experimenter Glück and the theorist Bug positioned themselves on the edges of different walls of the gorge (see Fig. 2). The line joining Glück and Bug makes an angle $\varphi=30^\circ$ with the horizontal. Glück and Bug threw identical balls with the same unknown initial speed $v_0$ relative to the Earth, and such that none of the thrown balls reached the opposite wall. The trajectories of the balls always lay in the vertical plane containing Glück and Bug. A moving ball is acted on by an air drag force directed opposite to the velocity of the ball and directly proportional to it. The sizes of Glück and Bug can be neglected.

After many experiments Glück and Bug found out the following:

• if a ball was thrown horizontally, it moved away horizontally to a distance $S$ from the thrower (see Fig. 1);
• when Glück and Bug simultaneously threw balls horizontally and at an angle $\alpha=60^\circ$ to the horizontal respectively (see Fig. 2), in the steady-state regime the balls move along one vertical straight line.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2024-2-1-fig1.png

[In the figures: Глюк = Glück, Баг = Bug; Рис. = Fig.]

Note: it is not required to give analytical answers that are functions of the angles $\alpha$ and $\varphi$.

1. Determine the distance $L$ between Glück and Bug (see Fig. 2).

2. For simultaneous throws by Glück and Bug of balls horizontally and at an angle $\alpha=60^\circ$ to the horizontal respectively, as shown in Fig. 2, determine the distance $S_\infty$ between the balls in the steady-state regime, and also the minimum distance $S_{min}$ between the balls during the motion.

problems.title: Problem 2: Collision on a rod
problems.problem:
Problem 2: Collision on a rod

Two identical small massless short cylinders can slide without friction along a long fixed horizontal rod. The cylinders are connected to massless inextensible threads 1 and 2, and the length of thread 1 is greater than the length of thread 2 by $L$ (see figure). A small bead of mass $m_1$ can move without friction along thread 1, and a small load of mass $m_2$ is attached to the ends of both threads. Initially the system consisting of the cylinders, threads, bead and load is held at rest in such a way that the rod and both threads lie in one vertical plane, the bead and the load are on one horizontal line, the bead is on one vertical line with the cylinder attached to thread 1, and the load is on one vertical line with the cylinder attached to thread 2. The threads are slightly taut. The free-fall acceleration is $g$. Assume that the sizes of the cylinders are larger than the sizes of the bead and the load. Air resistance can be neglected. The system is released.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2024-2-2-fig1.png

1. Determine the speeds $v_1$ and $v_2$ of the bead and the load respectively just before the collision of the cylinders.

2. Determine the tensions $T_1$ and $T_2$ of threads 1 and 2 respectively just before the collision of the cylinders.

problems.title: Problem 3: From the archive of the CSMC
problems.problem:
Problem 3: From the archive of the CSMC

In the 2011 archive of the CSMC (Central Subject-Methodological Commission) a problem was found that described a rather strange device for experiments with an ideal gas.

A thin-walled cylindrical tube of length $L$, closed at the bottom and placed vertically, is rigidly connected to a fixed cylindrical vessel whose axis is also vertical and whose diameter is many times larger than the diameter of the tube (see figure). The upper end of the tube is at a distance $l$ above the bottom of the vessel. A thin, light, airtight piston can move without friction in the tube. Under the piston there is air, which can be considered an ideal gas. In the upper part of the tube there are small stops that limit the motion of the piston upwards.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2024-2-3-fig1.png

There is a small hole in the wall of the vessel near its bottom. Using a thin tube through the hole, the vessel is very slowly filled with mercury, and then the mercury level in the vessel is lowered equally slowly down to its bottom.

Everywhere below, $h$ denotes the level of mercury in the vessel relative to the upper end of the tube, and $x$ is the distance between the piston and the stops. Assume that during the change of the mercury level in the vessel the temperature of the air under the piston and the atmospheric pressure remain constant.

Parameters of the setup: $L=3.04\,\mathrm{m}$, $l=0.04\,\mathrm{m}$; the atmospheric pressure $p_0$ is equal to the hydrostatic pressure of a mercury column of height $h_0=p_0/\rho g=0.76\,\mathrm{m}$, where $\rho$ is the density of mercury and $g$ is the free-fall acceleration. Consider the quantities $p_0$, $\rho$ and $g$ unknown.

In all parts of the problem give both analytical expressions and numerical values for the answers.

Initially there is no mercury in the vessel or above the piston, and the pressure of the air under the piston exceeds the atmospheric pressure. In parts 1–3 assume that when the mercury level in the vessel reached its maximum value $h_{max}=1.52\,\mathrm{m}$, the distance between the piston and the stops was $x_{max}=2.28\,\mathrm{m}$.

1. Consider the process of raising the mercury level in the vessel. At what value $h_1$ of the mercury level in the vessel did the piston start to move?

2. Let the mercury level in the vessel during its rise be $h_1+\Delta h$, where $0<\Delta h\ll h_1$. Find the possible values $x_1$ of the distance between the piston and the stops.

3. At what distance $x_2$ from the stops will the piston be when the mercury level in the vessel has been lowered to its bottom? Justify your answer.

4. The mercury was completely pumped out of the vessel and out of the space above the piston, after which the amount of air under the piston was changed. Then the processes of raising and lowering the level in the vessel using the thin tube through the hole were repeated. It turned out that when the mercury level in the vessel reached the value $h_{max}=1.52\,\mathrm{m}$, the distance between the piston and the stops was $x'_{max}=1.52\,\mathrm{m}$. At what value $h_2$ of the mercury level in the vessel does the piston reach the stops during the lowering process?

problems.title: Problem 4: Flights of a rod
problems.problem:
Problem 4: Flights of a rod

The experimenter Glück had at his disposal a fixed non-conducting sphere of radius $R$, uniformly charged over its surface with charge $Q$, and a very long thin straight non-conducting rod of mass $m$, uniformly charged along its length with linear charge density $\lambda$. It is known that the charges of the rod and of the sphere were of the same sign.

In the first series of experiments Glück placed the rod on the surface of the sphere so that the rod touched the surface of the sphere with its midpoint.

First Glück released the rod from rest, and when the distance between the centres of the sphere and the rod reached an unknown value $l>R$, the rod was moving with speed $u_0=\sqrt{Q\lambda/(2\pi\varepsilon_0 m)}$ (see Fig. 1).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2024-2-4-fig1.png

[Рис. = Fig.]

Then Glück began to set the rod in motion so that it started translational motion with various values of the initial velocity $v$ in the direction perpendicular to the rod and lying in the plane containing the rod and the centre of the sphere. Glück obtained the dependence on the initial speed $v$ of the rod of the time $\tau$ elapsed from the start after which the distance between the centres of the sphere and the rod reached an unknown value $S>R$ (see Fig. 2). The graph of the obtained dependence is given below in Fig. 3 in the coordinates $y(x)$, where $y=\tau/\tau_0$, $x=v/v_0$, and the quantities $\tau_0$ and $v_0$ are defined by the expressions:

$$\tau_0=R\sqrt{\frac{4\pi\varepsilon_0 m}{Q\lambda}},\qquad v_0=\sqrt{\frac{Q\lambda}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 m}}.$$

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2024-2-4-fig2.png

For the second experiment Glück made a small hole in the surface of the sphere, placed the end A of the rod inside the sphere so that it was at the centre of the sphere (see Fig. 4), and released the rod without initial velocity. There is no friction between the rod and the hole.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2024-2-4-fig3.png

In all experiments the rods moved translationally. The air drag force and gravity can be neglected. The quantities $S$ and $l$ are many times smaller than the length of the rod.

For the second experiment determine:

1. the time $T_1$ elapsed from the start after which the end A of the rod was at the surface of the sphere, and also the speed of the rod $V_1$ at that moment;

2. the speed $V_2$ of the rod at the moment when its end A was at the distance $l$ from the centre of the sphere;

3. the time $T$ elapsed from the start after which the end A of the rod was at the distance $S$ from the centre of the sphere.

problems.title: Problem 5: Electrotetrahedron
problems.problem:
Problem 5: Electrotetrahedron

An electric circuit is a tetrahedron, in two opposite edges of which there are the first and the second ideal sources of constant voltage with emfs $\mathcal{E}_1$ and $\mathcal{E}_2$ respectively. In the remaining edges there are four resistors $R_1$, $R_2$, $R_3$ and $R_4$ (see figure). The emfs of the sources and the resistance of one of the resistors are known: $\mathcal{E}_1=6\,\mathrm{V}$, $\mathcal{E}_2=12\,\mathrm{V}$, $R_2=3\,\Omega$. The magnitude of the current through the first source is $I_1=1\,\mathrm{A}$ and does not change when the polarity of connection of this source is reversed. The magnitude of the current through the second source with the polarity shown in the figure is $I_2=2\,\mathrm{A}$. The resistance of the connecting wires can be neglected.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2024-2-5-fig1.png

1. What will be the magnitude of the current through the second source if the polarity of the first source is reversed?

2. Find the magnitude of the current through the second source if: a) the first source is removed from the circuit; b) the first source is replaced by a jumper of zero resistance.

3. What are the resistances of the resistors $R_1$, $R_3$ and $R_4$?

problems.title: Problem 1: Accelerating mirror
problems.problem:
Problem 1: Accelerating mirror

The experimenter Glück holds in his hands a point light source S located under a horizontal plane mirror that moves translationally with a constant vertical acceleration. Glück threw the light source at an angle to the horizontal and began filming with a special video camera. Having analysed the video frame by frame, Glück plotted on a sheet of graph paper portions of the trajectories of the light source S and of its image $S^*$ in the mirror.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2024-3-1-fig1.png

Using the figure given, determine the magnitude and direction of the acceleration $\vec a$ of the mirror.

The free-fall acceleration is $g=9.80\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$. Air resistance can be neglected; consider the speed of light to be infinite.

The answer sheets contain a figure with the trajectories of the source and of the image on an enlarged scale. Carry out the necessary constructions on that sheet.

Note that the methods of finding the quantities needed for the solution will be assessed according to the accuracy of the proposed method.

problems.title: Problem 2: A powerful problem
problems.problem:
Problem 2: A powerful problem

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2024-3-2-fig1.png

[Рис. = Fig.]

The electric circuit whose diagram is shown in Figure 1 consists of an ideal source of constant voltage $U_0=12\,\mathrm{V}$, a resistor, an ideal diode (whose opening voltage is zero) and three devices, hereafter called "constant-power sources".

Denote by $I$ the electric current flowing through a device. The operating principle of a constant-power source is as follows:

1. At $I=1\,\mathrm{A}=I_u$, the device works as a source of constant current $I_u=1\,\mathrm{A}$, delivering a power not greater than the nominal power.

2. The device passes current only in the direction indicated by the arrow next to its symbol in the diagram. The current does not exceed $I_u$.

3. At $I\leqslant1\,\mathrm{mA}$ the device works as a source of constant voltage, delivering a power not greater than the nominal power and producing a voltage equal to $P/I_l$, where $P$ is the nominal power of the device and $I_l=1\,\mathrm{mA}$.

4. At $I_l<I<I_u$ the power delivered by the device is constant and equal to the nominal power.

5. The nominal power of the device is understood as $P=IU_V$, where the voltmeter reading $U_V>0$ (see Figure 2). Pay attention to the polarity of the voltmeter connection!

The nominal powers of the sources are: $P_1=1\,\mathrm{W}$, $P_2=2\,\mathrm{W}$ and $P_3=3\,\mathrm{W}$.

Find the values of the currents flowing in all branches of the circuit, and the resistance $R$ of the resistor. It is known that a current $I_R=0.8\,\mathrm{A}$ flows through the resistor.

In the solution use the following notation:

• $I_i$ is the electric current flowing through the device $P_i$;
• $I_D$ is the current through the diode;
• $I_0$ is the current through the constant-voltage source;
• $I_R$ is the current through the resistor.

problems.title: Problem 3: A nonlinear picture
problems.problem:
Problem 3: A nonlinear picture

A piece of ice of mass $m_i$ is put into a vessel and a portion of water of mass $m_w$ is poured in. The diagram shows the regions indicating the final state of the contents of the vessel depending on the temperature of the piece of ice $t_i\in[-100\,^\circ\mathrm{C};\,0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}]$ and the temperature of the portion of water $t_w\in[0\,^\circ\mathrm{C};\,100\,^\circ\mathrm{C}]$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2024-3-3-fig1.png

[In the diagram the axis labels tл and tв denote $t_i$ (temperature of the ice) and $t_w$ (temperature of the water); лёд = ice; смесь воды и льда = mixture of water and ice.]

It is known that in the range $[-100\,^\circ\mathrm{C};\,0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}]$ the specific heat capacity of ice depends on its temperature according to the law $c_i(t_i)=c+\alpha t_i$, where $c=2100\,\mathrm{J/(kg\cdot{}^\circ C)}$, $t_i$ is the temperature of the ice in degrees Celsius, and $\alpha$ is a certain constant. The specific heat capacity of water is $2c=4200\,\mathrm{J/(kg\cdot{}^\circ C)}$, and the specific latent heat of fusion is $\lambda=336\,\mathrm{kJ/kg}=2cT$, where $T=80\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$. Neglect the heat capacity of the vessel and heat losses.

1. Determine $\alpha$ and $\gamma=m_i/m_w$.

2. Sketch qualitatively an analogous diagram of the final state of the contents of the vessel depending on the temperature of the piece of ice $t_i\in[-100\,^\circ\mathrm{C};\,0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}]$ and the temperature of the portion of water $t_w\in[0\,^\circ\mathrm{C};\,100\,^\circ\mathrm{C}]$, but for equal masses of ice and water, $m_i=m_w$. Mark the characteristic points on the diagram.

problems.title: Problem 4: And when is it not taut?
problems.problem:
Problem 4: And when is it not taut?

A small massless ring can slide without friction along a long fixed horizontal rod. One end of a massless inextensible thread is attached to the ring, and the other end is fixed at a stationary point O (see figure). A massive bead can move without friction along the thread. Initially the thread is slightly taut, and the bead is on one horizontal line with point O and on one vertical line with the ring. The length of the horizontal portion of the thread is $L$. By a push the bead is set in motion in the vertical plane containing the thread. Immediately after the push the bead moves away from the rod, and the thread turns out to be taut. The free-fall acceleration is $g$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2024-3-4-fig1.png

1. At what angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal is the velocity of the bead directed immediately after the push?

2. For what values of the initial speed $v_0$ will the thread remain taut while the bead moves away from the rod?

problems.title: Problem 5: Removal from the ice
problems.problem:
Problem 5: Removal from the ice

Two identical small heavy boxes rest on the horizontal surface of ice. Both boxes are at the same distance $L=0.8\,\mathrm{m}$ from the straight edge of the ice field. A cleaner armed with a long scraper (a flat rectangular plate with handles) came up to the first box and pressed the edge of the scraper against one of the faces of the box. For this he turned the scraper so that its edge made an angle $\alpha_1=10^\circ$ with the edge of the field. Then he moved the scraper translationally from rest with a constant acceleration $a$ directed perpendicular to the edge of the field (see figure). As a result the box left the field in the time $t_1=2\,\mathrm{s}$. Then the cleaner came up to the second box and, acting in the same way, pushed it too beyond the edge of the field. He again moved the scraper translationally with the same acceleration, but this time the edge of the scraper made an angle $\alpha_2=45^\circ$ with the edge of the field. It is known that the coefficient of friction between the ice and both boxes is $\mu'=1/24$, and between the scraper and both boxes it is $\mu=7/24$. The free-fall acceleration is $g=10\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$. The scraper is vertical during the whole motion, and the box does not separate from the scraper.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2024-3-5-fig1.png

1. Determine the acceleration $a$ of the scraper.

2. How many times was the path of the second box to the edge of the field longer than that of the first box?

3. In what time $t_2$ will the second box leave the ice?

4. How many times is the friction force between the scraper and the second box greater than the friction force between the scraper and the first box?

problems.title: Problem 1: Two stones
problems.problem:
Problem 1: Two stones

From the top of a tower of height $h$, two stones are thrown simultaneously with equal speeds $v$, directed perpendicular to each other, at different angles to the horizontal, so that their motion takes place in one vertical plane. Some time after the throw, just before one of the stones hits the ground, it turned out that the velocity vectors of the stones were directed at equal angles to the horizontal.

Determine the magnitude of this angle $\varphi$ and the distance $l$ between the stones at this moment of time.

It is known that at the initial moment both stones are moving away from the surface of the ground, and just before one stone hits the ground the other stone is also approaching the surface of the ground. The tower stands on a horizontal surface. The acceleration due to gravity is $g$. Neglect air resistance.

problems.title: Problem 2: A cycle as a cycle
problems.problem:
Problem 2: A cycle as a cycle

In Lord Kelvin's archive, notes were found about a cycle consisting of four quasi-static processes $1-2$, $2-3$, $3-4$ and $4-1$ performed in succession by a classical ideal polyatomic gas. The graph of the cycle turned out to be lost, but it became known that in processes $1-2$ and $3-4$, on any small segment, the change in internal energy was exactly equal to the work done by the gas, and in processes $2-3$ and $4-1$, on any small segment, the change in internal energy was exactly equal to the work done by external forces on the gas.

The temperatures of three points of the cycle were given: $T_1=T_3=2T_0$, $T_4=T_0$. At point 4 the pressure and volume are $p_4=p_0$, $V_4=V_0$ respectively.

1. What was the temperature $T_2$ of the gas at point 2?

2. Reconstruct the graph of the cycle in the coordinates $\log_2\dfrac{p}{p_0}$ versus $\log_2\dfrac{V}{V_0}$.

3. Determine the efficiency of the cycle.

problems.title: Problem 3: Electrostatic levitation
problems.problem:
Problem 3: Electrostatic levitation

A vertical semi-infinite solid homogeneous dielectric cylinder of radius $R$ is charged with a charge density $\rho$ that is constant throughout its volume. A thin disc of thickness $d$ ($d\ll R$) was cut off the cylinder, then it was put back against it and released (see Fig. 1). The disc remained at rest, and it turned out that the only force of interaction between the disc and the cylinder is the force of electrostatic repulsion, equal in magnitude to

$$F_0=\frac{4}{3}\frac{\rho^2R^3d}{\varepsilon_0}.$$

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2025-1-3-fig1.png

Fig. 1

1. Find the density $D$ of the material of the cylinder.

2. The disc is given a velocity $v_0$, directed vertically upwards, such that it performs small oscillations, moving translationally. Determine the period of these oscillations.

Next, a small ring was cut off the disc and removed. The centre of the disc remained on the axis of the cylinder, and the new radius is $R'=R-\Delta R$, where $\Delta R\ll R$.

3. Determine the equilibrium position of the disc of radius $R'$. In your answer give the width $z_0$ of the gap between the disc and the cylinder in the equilibrium position.

4. Let the disc of radius $R'$ be in the equilibrium position. Determine the period of small oscillations of the disc in its translational motion along the axis of the cylinder after it is given the same velocity $v_0$ directed vertically upwards. If you have not done part 3, consider $z_0>0$ a known quantity.

Notes. The acceleration due to gravity is $g$. Assume that the disc can move only translationally along the axis of symmetry of the system, and that the bases of the disc are horizontal. There are no friction forces. Any possible collisions are perfectly elastic. Neglect the gravitational interaction of the disc and the cylinder, magnetism and electromagnetic radiation. Consider the dielectric to be non-polarisable.

problems.title: Problem 4: Glük's capacitor
problems.problem:
Problem 4: Glük's capacitor

At the very beginning of his career as an experimenter, Glük was keen on developing new devices. One of them was a capacitor of a rather unusual design. On the two surfaces of a rectangular glass plate of thickness $h=0.5\,\mathrm{mm}$ a metal coating (П) was deposited, playing the role of the capacitor plates. One side of the plate was completely covered with metal, the other only partially (Fig. 2). On the part free of coating a small droplet of conducting liquid (К) was placed, which does not wet glass at all. The conductor connected to the plate with the liquid branched so that one part of it was connected to the coated area, and the other end was immersed in the droplet of liquid.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2025-1-4-fig1.png

Fig. 2

[П — metal coating; К — droplet of liquid.]

In one of the experiments, Glük's capacitor was connected in series with another capacitor of constant capacitance (the reference capacitor) to an adjustable voltage source. The source voltage was increased smoothly from zero, and the dependence of the voltage $U_C$ across the reference capacitor on the source voltage $U$ was studied. The graph of this dependence consisted of two linear segments (Fig. 3), and the voltage across the reference capacitor at the kink point was one third of the source voltage $U_1$ corresponding to this point.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2025-1-4-fig2.png

Fig. 3

1. What was the voltage across the reference capacitor at a source voltage $U=2U_1$?

2. Determine the surface tension coefficient of the liquid used by Glük, if $U_1=5.9\,\mathrm{kV}$.

The electric constant is $\varepsilon_0=8.85\cdot10^{-12}\,\mathrm{F/m}$. The dielectric constant of glass is $\varepsilon=7$. The thickness of the glass plate is small compared with its dimensions. The surface tension coefficients of the liquid at the boundary with air and with glass are equal. The effect of gravity may be neglected.

problems.title: Problem 5: Two halves
problems.problem:
Problem 5: Two halves

On the principal optical axis (POA) of a thin converging lens of focal length $F$ there is a point monochromatic light source $S$ of wavelength $\lambda$. It is known that the diameter of the lens is $D$, with $\sqrt{\lambda F}\ll D\ll F$. The lens is cut into two identical halves (half-lenses), which are displaced parallel to their original positions (see Fig. 4) along the POA. One half (the upper one) ends up at a distance $d_1=4F/3$ from the source, and the other (the lower one) at a distance $d_2=2F$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2025-1-5-fig1.png

Fig. 4

[ГОО — principal optical axis.]

1. Find at what distances $l_1$ and $l_2$ from the source its images in the upper and lower half-lenses are located.

A screen is placed perpendicular to the POA at some distance $L$ from the source.

2. Describe the pattern observed on the screen (draw it schematically and determine the values of its essential characteristics) for $L_1=3F$ and $L_2=6F$.

3. At what distance $L_3>2F$ is an image in the form of a circle observed on the screen?

The screen is fixed at a distance $L_4=40F/9$ from the source.

4. Describe qualitatively and explain the pattern observed on the screen, indicating all its characteristic details.

5. Let us go from the point where the POA intersects the screen upwards, to the edge of the observed pattern. Determine how many intervals on this path there will be on which the illuminance of the screen increases. For the calculation use the values: $F=4\,\mathrm{m}$, $\lambda=650\,\mathrm{nm}$, $D=5\,\mathrm{cm}$.

Assume that the original lens was ideal: it had the property of tautochronism (rays from one source that have passed through different points of it reach the new point of intersection in the same time), and on passing through its focus the phase of the light wave changed abruptly by $\pi$.

All rays that do not fall directly from the source onto the half-lenses are cut off by diaphragms.

problems.title: Problem 1: The crossing
problems.problem:
Problem 1: The crossing

From point $A$, located on one bank of a river of width $l$, a small motorboat crosses to the opposite bank. The banks of the river are parallel to each other. The speed of the river current is the same everywhere and equal to $u$. On the opposite bank of the river, on the same perpendicular to the banks as point $A$, there is point $B$. The speed of the boat relative to the water is constant in magnitude and equal to $2u$, and its vector during the whole time of the crossing is perpendicular to the straight line $BC$, where $C$ is the centre of the boat. At some moment of time $t_1$ the velocity of the boat relative to the bank is perpendicular to the bank line.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2025-2-1-fig1.png

1. In which direction did the boat start its motion from point $A$: downstream or upstream? Justify your answer.

2. Find the angle $\angle ABC$ at the moment of time $t_1$.

3. At what distance from point $B$ will the boat be when it reaches the opposite bank of the river?

4. At what distance from point $B$ will the boat be at the moment of time $t_1$?

5. Find the radius of curvature of the trajectory of the boat in the reference frame of the bank for two cases: a) at the moment of the start from point $A$; b) at the moment of time $t_1$.

problems.title: Problem 2: The prism
problems.problem:
Problem 2: The prism

On the rough horizontal surface of a table there is a system consisting of a prism of mass $m$, equipped with a light pulley, and a block of mass $M=2m$ (see the figure). The lateral surface of the prism is smooth, and the angle between the face on which the block lies and the surface of the table is $\alpha$ ($\sin\alpha=3/5$). A light inextensible thread is tied to the block and passed over the pulley; a horizontal force $F$ is applied to its other end. It is known that the acceleration of the prism does not depend on the magnitude of this force.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2025-2-2-fig1.png

1. Determine the possible values of the coefficient of friction $\mu$ between the prism and the surface of the table.

2. For each of the values of $\mu$ obtained in part 1, find the acceleration $a$ of the prism.

The acceleration due to gravity is $g$. The inclined segment of the thread is parallel to the left lateral face of the prism. There is no friction in the axle of the pulley.

problems.title: Problem 3: The falling piston
problems.problem:
Problem 3: The falling piston

A cylindrical vessel, standing vertically in the gravitational field, contains a monatomic ideal gas under a massive horizontal piston of mass $m=100\,\mathrm{kg}$. Above the piston there is vacuum. The piston is in equilibrium and can move along the walls of the vessel practically without friction. The piston is fixed in this equilibrium position, after which a weight of mass $M$ is placed on it. Then the piston is released. In the subsequent motion of the piston with the weight, its minimum distance $h_{\min}$ from the bottom of the vessel is half the initial distance $h_0=1.0\,\mathrm{m}$. Determine:

1. the mass $M$ of the weight;

2. the magnitude of the maximum acceleration $a_{\max}$ of the piston with the weight during the motion;

3. the magnitude of the maximum speed $v_{\max}$ of the piston with the weight during the motion.

4. After a long time the piston came to rest. Find the distance $h$ from the bottom of the vessel at which the piston will be in the state of the new thermodynamic equilibrium.

The heat capacity of the vessel and the piston is negligible, and there is no heat transfer to the surroundings. During the motion of the piston from the initial position until its first stop, the processes in the gas may be considered to be equilibrium processes. The mass of the gas is much smaller than the mass of the piston. Take the acceleration due to gravity to be $g=10\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$.

problems.title: Problem 5: Vai kodamo!
problems.problem:
Problem 5: Vai kodamo!

In an infinite electric circuit, a fragment of whose diagram is shown in the figure, each triangular cell contains three sources with equal internal resistances $r$ but different EMFs ($\mathcal{E}$, $2\mathcal{E}$ and $3\mathcal{E}$), and the polarity of connection of the sources with the same EMF alternates periodically (see the figure).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2025-2-5-fig1.png

1. What are the potential differences $(\varphi_+-\varphi_-)$ between the plus and the minus of each source in this circuit?

2. Determine the currents through all the sources in this circuit.

3. What resistance $R_1$ will an ohmmeter show when connected to the plus and the minus of a source of EMF $\mathcal{E}$ in this circuit? What resistances $R_2$ and $R_3$ will the instrument show if the same is done with the sources $2\mathcal{E}$ and $3\mathcal{E}$ respectively? Will the readings of the ohmmeter depend on the polarity of its connection?

problems.title: Problem 1: Mach's slip
problems.problem:
Problem 1: Mach's slip

A microphone installed at point $A$ of a horizontal surface (see the figure) registered the signal from a supersonic aircraft a time $t$ after the aircraft flew over this point. After a further time $t$, the sound began to be registered by a microphone located at point $B$.

It is known that the first signal registered by microphone $B$ was emitted by the aircraft from point $C$. The aircraft moved uniformly and in a straight line in the same vertical plane as the microphones.

problems.title: Problem 2: Singularity
problems.problem:
Problem 2: Singularity

On a horizontal surface there are two bodies: a long board of height $h$ and a homogeneous cylinder of radius $R=2h$, which touch each other (see the figure). The mass of the cylinder is $M$. The coefficients of friction between the cylinder and the surface, and also between the bodies themselves, are the same and equal to $\mu$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2025-3-2-fig1.png

The board moves with a constant horizontal acceleration $a$, directed perpendicular to the line of contact with the cylinder. The acceleration due to gravity is $g$.

1. For what values of the acceleration $a$ of the board will the cylinder not rotate about a horizontal axis, if the coefficient of friction $\mu$ can take any values greater than zero?

problems.title: Problem 3: Three-body problem
problems.problem:
Problem 3: Three-body problem

In a galaxy far, far away, alien stations are able to attract spaceships located within their zone of action. The force of attraction $\vec F$ is directly proportional to the distance $\vec r$ from the station to the ship: $\vec F=-P\vec r$, where $P$ is the force coefficient of the station.

Three such stations are located at the vertices of a right triangle with an angle of $30^\circ$ and a hypotenuse of length $l$. The two stations located at the vertices of the acute angles are characterised by the force coefficient $P$, and the station at the vertex of the right angle by the force coefficient $2P$.

In parts 1–3 the space stations are stationary.

1. Determine the distances from each station to the point at which the ship will be in equilibrium.

At the initial moment of time a spaceship of mass $m$ is at the midpoint of the hypotenuse of the triangle at whose vertices the stations are located. The speed of the ship is zero, and the engines are off.

2. Determine the maximum speed $v_{\max}$ of the ship during its subsequent motion.

3. What is the minimum distance to which the ship will approach the station located at the vertex of the right angle during its motion?

The spaceship is again at the midpoint of the hypotenuse with zero initial velocity. However, at this moment the station at the vertex of the right angle begins to move with a constant speed $u=2v_{\max}$ along a straight line perpendicular to the initial direction towards the ship (see the figure). The stations located at the vertices of the acute angles remain stationary.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2025-3-3-fig1.png

4. After what time and at what distance from its initial position will the ship stop for the first time?

Note: all objects may be considered point-like; no forces act on the ship other than the forces of attraction from the stations.

problems.title: Problem 4: Hot–cold
problems.problem:
Problem 4: Hot–cold

The figure shows a fragment of the graph of the dependence on time $\tau$ of the average power $N_{\mathrm{av}}$, equal to the ratio of the total quantity of heat transferred to a silver ingot of mass $m=50\,\mathrm{g}$ to the time of its heat exchange with external bodies. Some time after the start of the heat exchange, the temperature of the ingot in state $A$ had increased to $t_A=40\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, and after a further $2.2\,\mathrm{min}$ (in state $B$) it was again equal to $t_A$. The specific heat capacity of silver is $c=240\,\dfrac{\mathrm{J}}{\mathrm{kg\,^\circ C}}$.

1. Reconstruct the coordinate axes of the graph and their scales, if it is known that the origin of the heating time axis coincides with the origin of the $N_{\mathrm{av}}$ axis.

2. Find the initial temperature $t_0$ of the silver ingot (at $\tau=0$).

3. Find the temperatures of the ingot and the average and instantaneous powers of heat exchange with external bodies in the states corresponding to points $C$ and $D$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2025-3-4-fig1.png

problems.title: Problem 5: A non-lamp diode
problems.problem:
Problem 5: A non-lamp diode

The figure shows the diagram of an electric circuit with an adjustable current source. Such a source delivers to the external circuit an electric current of a given magnitude, and the voltage at its outputs adjusts itself to the parameters of the external circuit.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2025-3-5-fig1.png

When a diode and a lamp connected in series are connected to the contacts $A$ and $B$, the reading of the ammeter is zero at two non-zero values of the current through the source, $I_{01}$ and $I_{02}$.

Assume that the current $I_{\mathrm{L}}$ flowing through the lamp and the voltage across it are related by:

$$I_{\mathrm{L}}=\alpha U_{\mathrm{L}}^{2/3}.$$

For the diode, the current $I_{\mathrm{D}}$ is proportional to the square of the voltage across it:

$$I_{\mathrm{D}}=\beta U_{\mathrm{D}}^2.$$

The resistances of the resistors $R_1$, $R_2$ and $R_3$, and also the coefficients $\alpha$ and $\beta$, are unknown.

1. At what non-zero value of the source current $I_{03}$ will the reading of the ammeter be zero if only the lamp is connected to points $A$ and $B$?

2. At what non-zero value of the source current $I_{04}$ will the reading of the ammeter be zero if only the diode is connected to points $A$ and $B$?

problems.title: Problem 1: Pothole
problems.problem:
Problem 1: Pothole

Experimenter Glyuk decided to learn to play the table game of air hockey. For this he bought all the necessary equipment and began to practise. However, to his surprise, he found that quite often after the puck is launched its trajectory differs from a straight line.

Glyuk decided to check what was the matter and discovered a deformation of the horizontal surface of the playing field: in one of its regions there was a round axially symmetric depression (a pothole) of radius $R$ with smooth edges and a horizontal bottom (see the figure).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2026-1-1-fig1.png

The experimenter decided to analyse how the puck is displaced when it passes through the pothole. For this he launched the puck perpendicular to the axis $OX$ (see the figure) from different initial positions with coordinate $x_0$ and measured the coordinate $x_1$ at which the puck leaves the pothole.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2026-1-1-fig2.png

As a result he obtained the following experimental points:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2026-1-1-fig3.png

The initial speed of all the launched pucks is $v_1$, the free-fall acceleration is $g$. There is no friction.

1. Determine the depth of the pothole.

2. Determine at what depth of the pothole Glyuk would always hit the goal when launching the puck from points with initial coordinates $|x_0|\ll R$.

Note

• Assume that the projections of the inclined parts of the pothole (its "walls") onto the horizontal plane are much smaller than the radius of the pothole, and that the puck never leaves the surface and is a point particle.

• The position of the goal is shown in the figure. Assume that its dimensions are small.

• For the geometric constructions and for obtaining the numerical values needed to solve the problem, use the graph printed on a separate sheet.

• Do not forget to hand in this sheet together with the others.

problems.title: Problem 2: Molecular physics
problems.problem:
Problem 2: Molecular physics

An ideal diatomic gas performs a cyclic process consisting of four successive segments: $1-2$, $2-3$, $3-4$ and $4-1$. Let $p$, $V$ and $n$ be the pressure, volume and concentration of the gas, and $p_0$, $V_0$ and $n_0$ some constant quantities, with $n_0V_0=N_0$, where $N_0$ is the unchanging number of gas molecules.

If this cycle is drawn on a state diagram in the coordinates $p/p_0$ (ordinate) and $V/V_0$ (abscissa), then the segments $1-2$ and $3-4$ are segments lying on straight lines passing through the origin. Point 2 has the largest ordinate in the cycle, and segment $4-1$ contains the point with coordinates $(1,1)$. The angles of inclination of segments $1-2$ and $3-4$ to the abscissa axis differ by $\alpha$. The scales of the axes on the graph are the same.

If the same cycle is drawn on a state diagram in the coordinates $p/p_0$ (ordinate) and $n/n_0$ (abscissa), then now the segments $2-3$ and $4-1$ are segments lying on straight lines passing through the origin. The scales of the axes on this graph are also the same.

It is known that the efficiency of the cycle of an ideal heat engine operating between the maximum and minimum temperatures reached during the given cycle is $\eta_K=0.5$.

1. Find the angles of inclination of the straight lines containing segments $2-3$ and $4-1$ on the state diagram in the coordinates $p/p_0-n/n_0$.

2. Draw (qualitatively) the cycle under consideration on a state diagram in the coordinates $n/n_0$ (ordinate) and $T/T_0$ (abscissa), where $T$ is the absolute temperature and $p_0=n_0kT_0$. Mark on the graph obtained the known points/point and values.

3. What values can the efficiency of this cycle take?

4. Find the range of possible efficiencies for the value of the angle $\alpha=\pi/3$.

5. Find the range of possible efficiencies for the value of the angle $\alpha=\pi/6$.

problems.problem:
Problem 3: Electrostatic study

On the axis of an infinite cylindrical cavity of radius $R$ with conducting walls there is an electric dipole with charges $q$ and $-q$ and arm $l$. At a distance $L$ from it, also on the axis, there is an electric charge $Q$. Here $l\ll R,L$. A force $F_Q$ acts on the charge $Q$. problems.title: Problem 4: Ring at the boundary
problems.problem:
Problem 4: Ring at the boundary

In a half-space a vertical uniform magnetic field of induction $B$ is created. On a smooth horizontal plane, touching the boundary of the region with the magnetic field, lies a rigid non-conducting thin ring of mass $m$ and radius $R$. The ring is uniformly charged with linear charge density $\lambda$. The ring is given some initial velocity, whose vector is horizontal and perpendicular to the boundary of the region with the magnetic field; before entering the region with the magnetic field the ring moves translationally.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2026-1-4-fig1.png

1. Let the initial velocity of the ring be such that it ends up entirely in the magnetic field. Determine the angular velocity of rotation of the ring immediately after this.

2. Determine the minimum value of the initial velocity $v_{\min}$ at which the ring will end up entirely in the region of the magnetic field.

The ring is given the velocity $v_0>v_{\min}$.

3. Determine the angle $\theta$ that the velocity vector of the centre of the ring makes with the boundary of the magnetic-field region immediately after the ring has completely crossed the boundary.

problems.title: Problem 5: RLC meter
problems.problem:
Problem 5: RLC meter

An $RLC$ meter is an instrument that allows one to measure resistances, inductances and capacitances directly. It contains a built-in generator of sinusoidal voltage, and also voltmeters that make it possible to measure the voltages across the terminals of the instrument and across a resistor connected to one of the terminals. In this way the instrument determines the ratio of the amplitudes of the current flowing through it and of the voltage at the terminals. From these measured values and the known frequency the value of the measured quantity (inductance, capacitance or resistance, depending on the mode) is calculated.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2026-1-5-fig1.png

Circuit of the $RLC$ meter

Experimenter Glyuk took a coil of inductance $L$ and a capacitor of capacitance $C$. In the first experiment he connected them in series, connected them to the $RLC$ meter and took readings in two operating modes. In the inductance-measuring mode the reading was $L_1=6.20\,\mathrm{mH}$, and in the capacitance-measuring mode $C_1=2.84\,\mathrm{\mu F}$. In the second experiment the same elements were connected in parallel and connected to the same instrument. In the inductance-measuring mode the instrument showed $L_2=21.3\,\mathrm{mH}$. The frequency was kept the same in all these measurements.

1. What value $C_2$ will the $RLC$ meter show in the capacitance-measuring mode in the second experiment? Obtain the formula and the numerical value.

2. What are the inductance $L$ and the capacitance $C$ of the coil and capacitor used by Glyuk? Obtain the formulas and the numerical values.

3. Now let the measurements be made for a non-ideal coil whose inductance is $L=10.0\,\mathrm{mH}$ and resistance $R=5.0\,\Omega$. For what values of the frequency $f$ at which the measurements are made is the error in determining the inductance associated with the resistance smaller than $0.1\,\%$? Assume that the real coil can be represented as an ideal coil and a resistor connected in series.

4. To the coil from the previous part Glyuk connected in series a capacitor of capacitance $C=1.00\,\mathrm{\mu F}$. The experimenter measured the inductance of the resulting circuit with the $RLC$ meter over the widest possible frequency range. Draw a qualitative graph of the measured values of the inductance as a function of frequency. Indicate the characteristic points and the asymptotic behaviour of the inductance as a function of frequency in the limits of low and high frequencies.

problems.title: Problem 1: Floating-up bar
problems.problem:
Problem 1: Floating-up bar

On the bottom of a vessel with a flat horizontal bottom lies a long uniform bar whose cross-section is a rectangle with sides $a$ and $b=a\sqrt{7}/3$ (see the figure). Water is slowly poured into the vessel.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2026-2-1-fig1.png

At what height $H$ of the water level in the vessel will the bar stop touching the bottom? The density of the material of the bar is $50\%$ of the density of water. The length of the bar is much greater than $a$. Because of the roughness of the surfaces of the bar and of the bottom of the vessel, water flows freely between them.

problems.title: Problem 2: Two against the wind
problems.problem:
Problem 2: Two against the wind

From a high but narrow bridge over a river, two identical balls were thrown simultaneously and practically from the same point $O$: the first at an angle $\alpha_1=10^\circ$ to the horizontal with speed $v_{10}=8\,\mathrm{m/s}$, the second at an angle $\alpha_2=50^\circ$ to the horizontal (see the figure).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2026-2-2-fig1.png

In the region of the bridge a strong horizontal wind is blowing, as a result of which, after a sufficiently long time, the balls began to move along parallel straight lines, all the time being on one vertical at a distance $L=6\,\mathrm{m}$ from each other. It is known that the first ball fell into the water $\tau=5\,\mathrm{s}$ after being thrown, and the second fell later. Assuming that the magnitude and direction of the wind velocity are the same everywhere and do not change with time, determine:

1. the initial speed of the second ball $v_{20}$;

2. the height $H$ of the bridge above the water surface;

3. the wind speed $u$, if it is known that both balls crossed the vertical passing through the point $O$ at the same distance from it.

The trajectories of both balls lie in one plane parallel to the vector $\vec{u}$. The force exerted on a ball by the air is given by the formula $\vec{F}=-k\vec{v}_{\text{отн}}$, where $\vec{v}_{\text{отн}}$ is the velocity of the ball relative to the air, and $k$ is a proportionality coefficient. Take the free-fall acceleration to be $g=10\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$.

Problem 3: Soda under a piston

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2026-2-3-fig1.png

A vertically positioned cylindrical vessel is divided into two equal parts, each of volume $V_0=6.6\,\mathrm{l}$, by a light horizontal gas-tight piston that can move without friction. The cross-sectional area of the vessel is $S=128\,\mathrm{cm^2}$. Both parts of the vessel contain equal amounts of carbon dioxide at pressure $P_0=164\,\mathrm{kPa}$ and temperature $T_0=274\,\mathrm{K}$.

At the moment of time $t=0\,\mathrm{s}$, cold water begins to flow slowly into the lower part of the vessel through a valve in its bottom at a constant volume flow rate $q=0.004\,\mathrm{l/s}$. The incoming water is constantly stirred so that the carbon dioxide dissolves in it up to the equilibrium state. The temperature of the water and of the gas in both parts of the vessel is kept constant and equal to $T_0$. The pump supplying the water stops working at the moment when the gas pressure in the upper part of the vessel reaches the value $P_{\text{кр}}=410\,\mathrm{kPa}$.

When carbon dioxide is above the surface of a liquid, the mass of $CO_2$ dissolved at temperature $T_0$ in $1\,\mathrm{m^3}$ of liquid in the equilibrium state is $\mu_{\text{р}}=k\cdot P$, where $k=3.17\cdot10^{-5}\,\mathrm{kg/(Pa\cdot m^3)}$, and $P$ is the partial pressure of the carbon dioxide in contact with the surface of the liquid (Henry's law).

The molar mass of carbon dioxide is $M=44\,\mathrm{g/mol}$, the universal gas constant is $R=8.31\,\mathrm{J/(K\cdot mol)}$. Neglect the saturated vapour pressure of water, the change in the volume of the water when the gas dissolves in it, and the volume of the valve.

1. With what speed and in what direction does the piston move at the initial moment of time?

2. After what time from the moment the pump is switched on is the minimum pressure in the upper part of the vessel reached?

3. Determine the minimum pressure in the upper part of the vessel during the operation of the pump.

4. How long did the pump work before it was switched off?

5. Draw the graph of the volume of gas in the upper part of the vessel as a function of time. Indicate on it the coordinates of the characteristic points.

Problem 4: Dumbbell in a cavity

In a very long non-conducting cylinder of radius $R$, uniformly charged throughout its volume, a cylindrical cavity of radius $R/2$ has been drilled. The axis of the cavity is parallel to the axis of the cylinder, and the distance between the axes is $R/2$. The cylinder is fixed in the gravitational field so that the plane passing through the axes of the cylinder and of the cavity is horizontal (Fig. a). It is known that a small ball of mass $m$, carrying a charge $q$ of the same sign as the charge of the cylinder, released without initial velocity from a point on the axis of the cavity, will hit the wall of the cavity after a time $\tau=\sqrt{\sqrt{2}R/(2g)}$, where $g$ is the free-fall acceleration.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2026-2-4-fig1.png

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2026-2-4-fig2.png

[The figure labels (а) and (б) are the Cyrillic letters for Fig. a and Fig. b.]

1. Determine the volume charge density $\rho$ of the cylinder.

In the cavity of the cylinder, a smooth non-conducting ring of radius $3R/8$ is fixed in a vertical plane so that the centre of the ring lies on the axis of the cavity. Two small beads are put on the ring and are connected by a hinged light rod of length $3\sqrt{2}R/8$. The charges and masses of the beads are $2q,m$ and $q,2m$ respectively. The system of the beads and the rod is held so that the rod is horizontal (Fig. b). The system is released, and it begins to move without friction along the ring.

2. Determine the maximum speed of the beads during their motion.

3. Determine the force with which the rod acts on a bead at the moment when the speed of the beads is maximum.

4. Determine the forces with which each of the beads acts on the ring at the moment when the speed of the beads is maximum.

The ring is far from the ends of the cylinder.

Problem 5: Thermistor, laser and diode

Tenth-grader Pasha, having become acquainted with the properties of a thermistor at the past regional stage, decided to assemble an electric circuit consisting of a source whose EMF can be adjusted, a resistor of resistance $r=40\,\Omega$, and a diode and a thermistor connected in parallel with each other (see Fig. 1). The EMF of the source can be varied in the range from $0\,\mathrm{V}$ to some sufficiently large value $\mathcal{E}_{max}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2026-2-5-fig1.png

Fig. 1

Pasha knows that the current–voltage characteristic of the diode has the form shown in Fig. 2, and the temperature dependence of the resistance of the thermistor is given by the formula

$$R(t)=R_0/(1+\alpha(t-t_0))^2,$$

where $R_0=60\,\Omega$ is the resistance of the thermistor at room temperature $t_0$ (the boy did not find the value of the constant $\alpha$). Having switched on the source and slowly increasing its EMF, Pasha found that the diode opens at a source EMF $\mathcal{E}_1=5\,\mathrm{V}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2026-2-5-fig2.png

Fig. 2

1. Continuing his experiments, Pasha took a powerful laser and began to shine it directly on the thermistor. It turned out that the diode then closed and, moreover, no changes of the source EMF led to its opening! Determine the minimum thermal power $P$ transferred in this case from the laser to the thermistor.

2. Having switched off the laser, Pasha found that the diode remained closed, even though the source EMF was close to $\mathcal{E}_{max}$. Surprised, the boy began to decrease the EMF smoothly. At what maximum value of the source EMF $\mathcal{E}_2$ will the diode open again?

The voltage across the open diode is $U_0=2\,\mathrm{V}$. The heat capacity of the thermistor and the internal resistance of the source can be neglected. The power of heat losses is proportional to the difference between the temperatures of the body and of the surroundings. In all the experiments the thermistor is in air at temperature $t_0$ and does not touch any other objects.

Problem 4: Heat exchanger

A heat exchanger consists of two coaxial pipes of length $L=5\,\mathrm{m}$. Through the inner pipe, in the positive direction of the $x$ axis, a mixture of water and ice flows with mass flow rate $\mu_{\text{х}}=0.70\,\mathrm{kg/s}$. Through the outer pipe, in the opposite direction, flows hot water with $\mu_{\text{г}}=0.50\,\mathrm{kg/s}$, whose temperature $T_{\text{г}}$ at $x=L$ is $60\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$. The heat exchanger is constructed so that the dependence of the mass fraction $\alpha(x)$ of ice on the coordinate $x$ has the form shown in the graph. The cross-sectional area of the inner pipe is constant and equal to $S=100\,\mathrm{cm^2}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/russia-2026-3-4-fig1.png

The specific latent heat of fusion of ice is $\lambda=3.35\cdot10^5\,\mathrm{J/kg}$, the specific heat capacity of water is $c=4.2\cdot10^3\,\mathrm{J/(kg\cdot K)}$, the densities of water and ice are $\rho_{\text{в}}=1000\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}$ and $\rho_{\text{л}}=900\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}$ respectively.
